articles.title: Dual-basket or countertop oven? Start with the meal, not the quart number
articles.standfirst: Two small drawers and one oven cavity organise a meal differently. Here is what the documents establish before cooking performance enters the question.
articles.target_query: dual basket vs air fryer oven

sections.h: Two foods, or one oven cavity?
paras: The Chefman dual-window model divides {{6 Qt / 5.67 L}} between {{Two 3-quart baskets::two 3-quart baskets}}. Its manual lets you set the baskets separately and use Sync Finish to delay the shorter cook so the timers finish together.

The Emeril is a countertop oven documented at {{26 qt / 24.6 L (manual: 1,519 cu in)}}. The FAFO-001 manual names toast, bake and rotisserie presets. Those are different arrangements of space and controls, not evidence that one cooks better.

sections.h: A shared finish time is not a doneness guarantee
paras: Sync Finish coordinates timers. The Chefman manual still says to check food for doneness; pressing Hi-Fry or +2 MIN breaks the sync. An oven also needs the right accessory position and cooking instructions for the food. Neither a timer nor a preset removes those checks.

sections.h: Measure the operating space, not just the body
paras: The dual-window body is listed at {{13.38 × 11.81 × 10.63 in / 33.98 × 30 × 27 cm}}. The Emeril brand page lists {{16.9 D × 15.8 W × 14.8 H in}}.

The Emeril manual requires free space around the appliance and says not to operate it under hanging cabinets. A body fitting into a gap does not establish that it can be used there. Read the full clearance instructions for the exact model.

sections.h: A practical way to choose
paras: Editorial judgement: start with the meal you regularly make. Separate settings may be useful for two components; an oven cavity may suit a task requiring its documented rack or rotisserie arrangement. Then check the exact model, accessory limits and usable space. The nominal capacity alone cannot tell you how many portions will fit.

articles.closing_note: Documentation can establish a feature or an instruction, not how well this appliance performed in a kitchen. No hands-on testing is claimed.

articles.title: What “450 °F” actually means on an air-fryer listing
articles.standfirst: A temperature badge may describe a brief finishing mode rather than the setting for a whole cook. The model code and manual matter more than the badge.
articles.target_query: air fryer 450 degrees hi-fry meaning

sections.h: Read the time limit beside the temperature
paras: The dual-window Chefman page publishes {{200–450 °F / 95–235 °C}}. Its RJ38-SQPF-3TDB-2W manual describes Hi-Fry more narrowly: {{450 °F / 235 °C, held for 2 minutes, for extra browning}}.
That instruction supports a short finishing boost. It is not evidence that the normal cooking controls hold that temperature for an entire cycle.

sections.h: Two 8-quart pages do not describe one interchangeable model
paras: The stainless RJ38-SQSS-8T is documented at {{200–400 °F}}. Chefman separately lists RJ38-8T-BLACK with a Hi-Fry button for the final two minutes and four named cooking functions.
A feature on the second page cannot be transferred to the first because their names are similar. Nor does the existence of both pages establish which unit an unconfirmed Amazon listing supplies.

sections.h: What the listing conflict does—and does not—prove
paras: The dated listing observation in this repository describes a stainless 8-quart unit with a 450 °F Hi-Fry option. It does not settle the relationship to the two manufacturer models. A stale title, a variant difference or another explanation remains unconfirmed; this site assigns no probability to them.

sections.h: Before buying
paras: Find the selected variant and model number, then compare them with the manufacturer page and matching manual. Ask the seller or manufacturer if they disagree. If the feature is essential and the identity cannot be confirmed, do not rely on the badge alone. Higher temperature by itself is not a tested browning result.

articles.closing_note: Documentation can establish a feature or an instruction, not how well this appliance performed in a kitchen. No hands-on testing is claimed.

sections.h: The page does not use one counting system
paras: The Emeril brand page has described the French-door oven as 10-in-1, used 25 Cooking Pre-sets in its specification block and 24 one-touch cooking presets in the description. These statements are not interchangeable definitions of a cooking function.

sections.h: The manual supplies a countable list
paras: The FAFO-001 manual names {{24 presets are named in the owner's manual for model FAFO-001: Airfry, Fries, Bacon, Grill, Eggs, Fish, Ribs, Defrost, Steak, Vegetables, Wings, Bake, Rotisserie, Toast, Chicken, Pizza, Pastry, Proof, Broil, Slow Cook, Roast, Dehydrate, Reheat, Warm}}.
The chart also distinguishes temperature ranges, fan settings and accessory positions. Those details are more useful for a particular task than the total on the sales page.

sections.h: What is still unresolved
paras: The manual list can be reported for FAFO-001 without declaring the marketing count correct. The repository also records different model strings on the manual, brand page and listing. The list is not proof that an unidentified purchase will have that exact control panel.

sections.h: Choose the task, then read its row

articles.title: Two 3-quart drawers or one 8-quart basket: which fits your meals?
articles.standfirst: Six quarts split in two is not eight quarts in one basket. Capacity describes the container; your menu determines whether the split is useful.
articles.target_query: dual basket vs single basket air fryer

sections.h: Start with the actual difference in capacity
paras: The dual-window Chefman is {{6 Qt / 5.67 L}} in {{Two 3-quart baskets::two 3-quart baskets}}. The single-basket product page covers an {{8 qt (brand also sells a 5 qt version of the same product page)}} model.
Arithmetic: eight quarts is one-third more nominal capacity than six. That is not a one-third increase in portions or usable cooking area. The shapes, food and loading instructions also matter.

sections.h: What the second drawer buys you
paras: The manual allows separate settings and documents Sync Finish, which delays the shorter cook so the timers end together. Sync Baskets instead copies the same settings to both drawers. Those are scheduling features, not a promise about food temperature or doneness.

sections.h: What one large basket changes
paras: One compartment avoids dividing the nominal capacity between two drawers. It may be relevant when the item you want to cook must fit in one basket, but the quart figure does not establish that a particular chicken, pan or quantity fits.
Chefman describes the single-basket model as {{Designed for 4–6 people::designed for 4–6 people}}. That is the manufacturer’s household-size description, not a portion test by this publication.

sections.h: Try this menu check
paras: Editorial judgement: list a few ordinary dinners. Do their components need different settings? Does one item need a single large space? Then read the matching manual’s loading guidance. Both Chefman manuals warn against overcrowding and recommend checking doneness. Neither nominal capacity nor a synced finish answers how much your household will eat.

articles.closing_note: Documentation can establish a feature or an instruction, not how well this appliance performed in a kitchen. No hands-on testing is claimed.

articles.title: Chefman 6 Qt Dual Basket: what the documents establish
articles.standfirst: Two drawers, separate settings and a short Hi-Fry finish. This is a guide to model RJ38-SQPF-3TDB-2W, not a report from a test kitchen.
articles.target_query: chefman 6 quart dual basket air fryer review

sections.h: The documented format
paras: The manufacturer lists {{6 Qt / 5.67 L}} split into {{Two 3-quart baskets::two 3-quart baskets}}. The body is listed at {{13.38 × 11.81 × 10.63 in / 33.98 × 30 × 27 cm}} and {{13.3 lb / 6.03 kg}}.
Those are manufacturer specifications. They do not measure usable food capacity, noise, cooking evenness or how comfortable the baskets are to handle.

sections.h: The useful feature is the schedule
paras: Sync Finish delays the shorter cook so the two timers finish together. Sync Baskets copies the first basket’s settings to the second. Pulling a basket during a sync cook pauses both; the manual also explains which adjustments break the sync.
Editorial judgement: this layout is worth considering if separate settings solve a real meal-planning problem. It is not automatically preferable for one large item.

sections.h: Do not read Hi-Fry as a whole-cycle setting
paras: The product page states {{200–450 °F / 95–235 °C}}. The manual describes the Hi-Fry button as {{450 °F / 235 °C, held for 2 minutes, for extra browning}}. Neither passage establishes a proofing or dehydrating function at the lower end.

sections.h: Care and identity checks before a purchase
paras: The manual prohibits aerosol cooking-oil spray on the baskets and racks, permits a non-aerosol mister and says cooled baskets and racks are top-rack dishwasher safe. Follow the complete instructions, including cooling and non-submersion warnings.

This guide describes the named manufacturer model. It does not certify that the submitted short link supplies it. Confirm the selected listing, model and accessories before relying on these specifications.

articles.title: How to read an air-fryer spec sheet in a useful order
articles.standfirst: Find the model, check the operating space, then read the feature you actually need. A long specification list is not the same as an answer.
articles.target_query: how to read air fryer specifications

sections.h: Begin with identity, not the largest number
paras: Write down the exact model on the manufacturer page and matching manual. A page covering several sizes needs a second check: the Chefman single-basket page, for example, publishes separate 5-quart and 8-quart dimensions.
A listing title is not an official cross-reference. If the model or selected variant is uncertain, treat any comparison built on it as provisional.

sections.h: Check the space in which it operates
paras: Outer dimensions are only the start. Read the clearance, ventilation, surface and cord instructions. The Emeril manual says not to operate under hanging cabinets; the Chefman 8-quart manual gives its own top and rear clearance.
Weight matters if you plan to move the cooled appliance for storage. Do not assume that a catalogue or shipping weight describes the unboxed unit.

sections.h: Read capacity and temperature in context
paras: A total capacity split between two drawers is not one continuous space. A peak temperature used briefly is not a full-cycle setting. The dual-window Chefman’s Hi-Fry mode is limited to two minutes; the FAFO-001 oven has a chart with different ranges for different presets.
Choose the function you need and read its row rather than comparing only maximums and preset totals.

sections.h: Finish with care, warranty and the unanswered questions
paras: Check which removable parts can go in a dishwasher, which sprays or cleaners are prohibited and what the warranty actually covers. None of that establishes that a coating will survive a particular number of years.

Editorial checklist: exact model, operating space, electrical requirements, compartment shape, function instructions, accessory limits, cleaning and warranty. If a document does not answer a question, keep it open rather than supplying a plausible answer.

articles.closing_note: Documentation can establish a feature or an instruction, not how well this appliance performed in a kitchen. No hands-on testing is claimed.

articles.title: What an air-fryer capacity number can—and cannot—tell you
articles.standfirst: Quarts help compare nominal scale. They do not establish a serving count, the size of a whole item or how evenly a full basket cooks.
articles.target_query: 26 quart air fryer capacity

sections.h: The three published capacities
paras: The dual-window Chefman is {{6 Qt / 5.67 L}} as {{Two 3-quart baskets::two 3-quart baskets}}. The single-basket page documents an {{8 qt (brand also sells a 5 qt version of the same product page)}} model. The Emeril is listed as {{26 qt / 24.6 L (manual: 1,519 cu in)}}.
These are manufacturer capacity figures. This publication has not filled or measured the appliances.

sections.h: A split capacity cannot be used as one cavity
paras: Two 3-quart drawers do not make a drawer large enough for a 6-quart object. A single 8-quart basket is also not the same nominal total as the dual unit. Neither figure provides the basket’s usable food dimensions.
The manuals warn against overcrowding and explain loading. Food quantity and spacing cannot be recovered from the quart figure alone.

sections.h: Keep a household claim attached to its author
paras: Chefman describes the single-basket model as {{Designed for 4–6 people::designed for 4–6 people}}. That remains the brand’s description. It does not establish portions for another model, another food or a particular family.

sections.h: Ask the question the volume does not answer
paras: Will your usual item fit in the usable space, with the required circulation and accessory arrangement? The 8-quart manual provides suggested food quantities and timings for particular foods; these are suggestions, not a universal capacity guarantee.

Editorial judgement: use capacity to narrow the format, then consult the exact manual and usable dimensions. The largest nominal cavity is not necessarily the right purchase for the meal or the counter.

articles.closing_note: Documentation can establish a feature or an instruction, not how well this appliance performed in a kitchen. No hands-on testing is claimed.

articles.title: Will it fit? Start with dimensions, then read the clearance rules
articles.standfirst: A body fitting on a counter is not proof it can safely operate there. Keep the manufacturer’s dimensions and operating instructions together.
articles.target_query: air fryer dimensions counter space

sections.h: Write down the dimensions from the right variant
paras: The dual-window Chefman is listed at {{13.38 × 11.81 × 10.63 in / 33.98 × 30 × 27 cm}}. The 8-quart Chefman’s combined row is {{8 Qt model: 15.4 × 12.6 × 13.5 in / 39.11 × 32 × 34.29 cm · 12.8 lb / 5.8 kg}}. The Emeril page lists {{16.9 D × 15.8 W × 14.8 H in}}.
The Chefman page separates its 5-quart and 8-quart figures. Do not take one model’s measurements from the other variant’s row.

sections.h: Add the operating space
paras: The Chefman 8-quart manual calls for at least 6 inches of clearance on the top and back. The Emeril manual calls for at least 5 inches of free space around the top, back and sides and separately says not to operate under hanging cabinets.
These are different instructions for different units. A single clearance number cannot be substituted for the complete manual. Allow for access to drawers, doors, controls and the outlet as well.

sections.h: Do not turn dimensions into a cooking-efficiency score
paras: No useful “capacity per square inch” ranking follows without knowing the dimension order, usable food area and operating clearance. A nominal volume divided by a body footprint would not measure food capacity or performance.

sections.h: Before you choose the spot
paras: Check the exact unit’s manual, the surface requirements and any cabinet or counter restrictions. The repository records conflicting dimensions for the unconfirmed 8-quart listing; manufacturer figures do not resolve that listing identity.
Editorial judgement: leave the placement decision open if the model or measurements remain uncertain. This guide is not an electrical installation or countertop heat-resistance assessment.

An original diagram or an AI-generated food scene is not a product photograph or proof of an outcome. The visual labels and editorial-method page explain that distinction.

sections.h: What to look for in any guide
paras: Editorial checklist: a visible financial disclosure, a clear account of how the material was made, sources next to factual claims and an honest description of the limits. Treat a documented feature, an author’s judgement and a measured result as different kinds of statement.

articles.title: What a 1,700-watt rating tells you about energy cost
articles.standfirst: Nameplate power is not energy measured over a cooking cycle. The missing ingredient in a running-cost claim is the actual consumption.
articles.target_query: air fryer wattage 1700w circuit

sections.h: Power is a rating, not a bill
paras: The Chefman pages publish {{1700 W / 120 V}}; the FAFO-001 manual lists {{1700 W}} at {{120 V / 60 Hz}}. These are the manufacturers’ electrical ratings, not measured average draw during a meal.
Compatibility, circuits and outlets need the exact manual and an appropriate electrical assessment. This article does not decide whether a particular circuit can run another appliance.

sections.h: The cost calculation needs energy
paras: Energy cost is measured kilowatt-hours multiplied by the applicable price per kilowatt-hour. Converting the nameplate figure gives 1.7 kilowatts; multiplying that by elapsed hours would assume the full rated power for the whole interval.

That assumption is not a consumption measurement. It should not be presented as the precise cost of a cook. Your tariff and the appliance’s actual operation remain inputs, not facts supplied by this site.

sections.h: No oven-savings comparison follows from size alone
paras: The specifications do not contain a matched cooking test against a full-size oven. They cannot establish which uses less energy for a particular meal. Cooking time, preheating, load and the comparison appliance would all have to be part of the test.

sections.h: What to check instead
paras: Read the appliance’s supply and cord instructions before using it. For an energy comparison, use trustworthy measured data for the relevant task rather than a percentage inferred from cavity size. This publication has no such measurement and publishes no savings estimate.

articles.closing_note: Documentation can establish a feature or an instruction, not how well this appliance performed in a kitchen. No hands-on testing is claimed.

articles.title: Sync Finish: what it coordinates, and what breaks the sync
articles.standfirst: The manual describes a scheduling feature, not a promise that two different foods will be safely cooked at the same instant.
articles.target_query: air fryer sync finish explained

sections.h: Sync Finish delays the shorter cook
paras: For RJ38-SQPF-3TDB-2W, the manual says to set each basket, select Sync Finish and start. The longer cook begins first; the other basket displays HOLD until its delayed start.
Sync Baskets is different: it copies the same time and temperature to both baskets. It is a shortcut for matching settings, not a second name for staggered starts.

sections.h: Basket removal pauses both in the sync modes
paras: The sync instructions say that removing one basket pauses both sides until the basket is returned. That behaviour matters when checking or turning food. The same passage describes the shake reminder; it does not remove the cook’s responsibility to inspect the food.

sections.h: More than two buttons can break Sync Finish
paras: Hi-Fry and +2 MIN break sync. The Sync Finish steps also say that adjusting either timer while both sides are actively cooking breaks sync; the two baskets continue cooking, but the shared schedule no longer applies.

While one basket is still waiting, the finish remains synced only under the manual’s stated condition: the shorter time must not be increased above the longer one. Read the complete sequence rather than assuming all mid-cook changes preserve the schedule.

sections.h: A finish time is not a food-safety result
paras: The manual instructs the cook to check both baskets for doneness. Different quantities and foods may need more time even when the timers end together.

Editorial judgement: use Sync Finish when coordinating separate settings is useful, but do not treat its name as a replacement for checking food. This publication has not tested the timing or cooking result.

articles.closing_note: Documentation can establish a feature or an instruction, not how well this appliance performed in a kitchen. No hands-on testing is claimed.

articles.title: The aerosol-oil warning appears in both Chefman manuals
articles.standfirst: The two manuals use different wording, but both caution against aerosol spray on nonstick parts. An earlier article incorrectly said the 8-quart manual had no rule.
articles.target_query: aerosol cooking oil air fryer nonstick coating

sections.h: The dual-window wording
paras: The RJ38-SQPF-3TDB-2W manual cautions against spraying the baskets or racks with cooking oil from an aerosol can because harsh components can chip the coating. It says they may be oiled or sprayed from a non-aerosol mister.
This is the manufacturer’s care instruction, not a coating-durability test by this publication.

sections.h: The 8-quart wording is explicit too
paras: The RJ38-SQSS-8T manual states: “Never use aerosol spray on the air fryer’s nonstick parts as it can cause the coating to chip.” The next sentence allows oil from a mister.
That warning is in the operating instructions, not only the cleaning section. The shorter care row in this site’s dataset did not prove that the manual lacked the instruction.

sections.h: The oil instructions do not stop there
paras: Both manuals also say not to fill the baskets with oil and describe lightly oiling food separately where appropriate. Their cooking tips discuss food-specific use. It would be inaccurate to say that the only oil instruction is a spray-can warning, or that no quantities are ever suggested.

sections.h: Use the instructions for the exact model
paras: Check the manual supplied with your unit, including cooling, washing and non-submersion instructions. Do not transfer a permission or prohibition to a different appliance just because the coating looks similar. Following a care instruction is not a promise of a particular service life.

articles.closing_note: Documentation can establish a feature or an instruction, not how well this appliance performed in a kitchen. No hands-on testing is claimed.

articles.title: The Emeril manual contradicts itself about extension cords
articles.standfirst: One safeguard says never to use an extension cord; the power-cord section later describes using one. This is a safety question for the manufacturer, not an ambiguity to resolve by preference.
articles.target_query: air fryer 1700 watts extension cord manual

sections.h: Both passages are in the same manual
paras: In the FAFO-001 manual’s Important Safeguards, item 9 says: “NEVER use with an extension cord.” In the later Attaching the Power Cord section, it says longer extension cords are available and may be used with care, then lists conditions.
The earlier article quoted only the first passage and called the rule absolute. The source does not support that description of the complete document.

sections.h: What this publication will not infer
paras: The later passage does not give this site authority to cancel the earlier prohibition. The contradiction is recorded on the Flagged page and remains unresolved. Do not rely on this article as permission to use an extension cord; obtain clarification from the manufacturer for the exact unit and seek qualified electrical advice where needed.

sections.h: The Chefman manuals are separate instructions
paras: The two cited Chefman manuals describe longer cords subject to care, an adequate marked electrical rating and routing that avoids pulling or tripping hazards. That wording applies to those manuals; it cannot resolve the Emeril contradiction.
The appliances’ shared nominal wattage is not a reason to give them one shared set of operating instructions.

sections.h: Plan the location before the purchase
paras: Check the outlet, supply and placement instructions for the exact model before buying. The Emeril document also calls for a dedicated outlet/circuit, ventilation space and no operation under hanging cabinets.
This article reports the conflicting document. It is not an installation guide, a cord recommendation or a finding that either passage is the intended final instruction.

articles.title: What the Amazon Associate disclosure does—and does not—say
articles.standfirst: The sentence identifies a financial relationship. It does not certify the link, the publisher’s account or the accuracy of a product claim.

sections.h: The wording comes from the Operating Agreement
paras: Section 5 requires the statement “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.”, or a substantially similar statement previously allowed under the agreement, to be clearly and prominently placed.
This publication uses the prescribed sentence verbatim beneath its masthead and in its footer. The agreement also says not to misrepresent Amazon’s support, sponsorship or endorsement.

sections.h: Placement matters as well as wording
paras: The FTC’s disclosure guidance says a material connection should be obvious and hard to miss. It warns against placing the only disclosure on an About page or where someone must click to reveal it.

Editorial implementation: the site-wide statement remains visible before the main content, and affiliate-link text explains the potential commission near the action. That is not a declaration of legal compliance for every jurisdiction or medium.

sections.h: It does not establish attribution
paras: A statement on this page cannot prove that a supplied link is a properly formed, enrolled Special Link, or that an order has been credited. The selected tracking ID remains unconfirmed and the campaign ledger contains no report rows.
The account and exact-product checks are recorded separately in the intent register. No earnings follow merely from displaying the sentence.

sections.h: It does not license unsupported endorsements
paras: The FTC says not to describe product experience you do not have. Amazon separately restricts its prices, customer reviews and star ratings. A disclosure does not waive those rules.
The content here is documentation-based and AI-assisted, not a first-hand recommendation from a named tester. The editorial-method page describes that limit.

paras: Both Chefman manuals say to unplug and allow the unit to cool completely before cleaning. The Emeril manual also requires cooling and gives a minimum wait in its operating cautions.

articles.title: “98% less oil”: what would make the claim checkable?
articles.standfirst: The Chefman page publishes the percentage. A useful reading separates the manufacturer’s wording from a measured comparison this site has not performed.
articles.target_query: air fryer 98% less oil meaning

sections.h: Keep the claim attached to the source
paras: Chefman’s single-basket product page uses the phrase “98% less oil”. The evidence dataset labels it as a brand claim. It is not a result measured by this publication.

The product copy read for this review does not supply enough detail to reproduce that percentage: a named baseline, matched food and quantity, method and measurement record would be needed. This does not establish that no supporting material exists elsewhere.

sections.h: Do not turn an unclear comparison into a health conclusion
paras: The percentage alone does not establish nutrition, a benefit for a particular person or equivalence between cooking methods. This site makes no finding about whether the wording is legally a health claim.
The FTC’s guidance warns against making claims that require proof the advertiser does not have. An affiliate publisher should not enlarge a marketing sentence into a result it has not substantiated.

sections.h: The manuals contain practical oil instructions too
paras: Both Chefman manuals warn against filling the baskets with oil and describe lightly oiling food where appropriate. Both also caution against aerosol spray on nonstick parts and permit a mister.

The manuals include food-specific advice and suggested quantities. The earlier version’s claim that no such quantity appears was wrong. Care guidance and a quantified marketing comparison are different kinds of statement.

sections.h: Four questions worth keeping
paras: Compared with what? On which food and quantity? Who measured it, using which method? Is the supporting comparison available to read?

Editorial judgement: until those questions have useful answers, report the sentence as the manufacturer’s claim rather than your own finding. A large percentage is not a substitute for a defined comparison.

articles.title: Eight questions before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
articles.standfirst: A short checklist for turning a long feature list into a buying decision—with room to leave an answer unresolved.
articles.target_query: questions to ask before buying a multi function air fryer oven

sections.h: First: identity and operating space
paras: **1. Which exact model and selected variant is this?** Match the full code to the manufacturer page and manual; a similar name is not enough.

**2. Can it operate where you intend to put it?** Read the surface, ventilation, clearance and door or drawer access instructions, not just the body dimensions. The Emeril manual separately prohibits operation under hanging cabinets.

sections.h: Next: the food and function
paras: **3. Is the capacity one usable space or split into compartments?** A total volume is not an item-fit measurement or serving guarantee.

**4. What does the advertised mode actually do?** Read its time limit, setting range and conditions. A two-minute Hi-Fry finish is not a whole-cycle temperature; Sync Finish coordinates timers, not doneness.

sections.h: Then: the parts and routine
paras: **5. Which required accessories are included in this offer?** The oven manual lists parts but also says some may not be included. Check the particular item and its load limit.

**6. Does the care routine suit you?** Find the instructions for cooled removable parts, the appliance body, prohibited sprays and cleaners. Do not extend one model’s instruction to another without reading it.

sections.h: Finally: supply and unresolved claims
paras: **7. Are the electrical and placement instructions clear for the exact unit?** The FAFO-001 manual contains contradictory extension-cord passages. That requires manufacturer clarification, not an editorial guess.

**8. What important question is still unanswered?** Cooking evenness, noise or durability needs appropriate evidence. No appliance was tested for this publication. If model identity or a necessary instruction remains unclear, the decision can stay open.
